name: Madame Traction
role: Fixer, rumour-broker, purveyor of grip tape and foreknowledge
bio: Keeps a two-chair shop under the third mooring mast in Keel Town, wedged between a rope-seller and a woman who recanes deck chairs. Sells grip tape, choke leathers, boot hooks — and, from the drawer beneath the till, information, priced by how much it will cost you to know it. She knew about the ledger-entry that wrote itself onto the Driftline's manifest a week before Ash Varga was handed the crate. She has said this to no one. She is waiting to see whether the universe asks nicely.
appearance: A compact woman of indeterminate years in a storm-grey coat sewn over with sample loops of every grip tape she has ever stocked, like plumage; amber cabochon glasses on a chain, coins braided into grey hair, and hands permanently faintly silvered with the adhesive she calls 'the honest work'.
voice: Noir with a shop bell on it. Speaks in prices, proverbs, and SKU numbers; never lies, frequently declines to be helpful for free. Calls everyone 'dear' in the tone of a closing lid. Believes friction — physical, commercial, moral — is the only thing standing between civilisation and the long slide.

greetings: Grip tape, boot hooks, choke leathers — and for the discerning courier, the drawer. Sit, dear. The chair is free. Everything after the chair is priced.
Ash Varga. You're the one carrying the parcel nobody wrote down. Tape first, questions later. Tape always first.
A courier with that much dust and that little trouble? You've come for the drawer.
barks: Everything in Keel Town is moored, dear, except a secret. Secrets drift. I merely net them.
Guild sells what things cost. Choir sells what things mean. I sell what things *did*.
The third mast creaks before bad news arrives. It creaked Tuesday. You're my Wednesday. Fascinating.
mission: A matter, courier: three manifest stubs from my stock have gone walking, and they walk toward the Guild exchange. Fetch them back before someone learns taxes I never charged.
Deliver this reel of widow-black tape to the winch yard and let no one read the label. Reading the label voids the warranty on the whole errand, dear.
There's a rumour about your crate with my name on it. Retrieve the rumour. No — you may not listen to it. Yes — I'll know if you did.
radio: Traction on the trade band: a reminder that information, like tape, bonds under pressure and peels in heat. Season's approaching, dears.
To the courier asking around about ledgers that write themselves: entries can't write themselves, dear. They can only be *continued*. Shop's open.
This week's forecast: dust, temptation, and a minor shortage of people who ask twice. Stock accordingly.
crate: Your crate has a manifest stub, Varga. Every crate does; that's the system. Yours predates the manifest. That's the *drawer*.
Someone wrote your parcel into being the way you'd mend a rope: splice, wrap, pray. I know the tension pattern. I taught half this town to tie it.
Three factions have asked me what that box is. I sell answers by weight, me, and that one — that one I decline to pick up. So do you, if you're wise. You're not. That's why I like you.
rumours: Current stock, dear: who bought the missing courier's tabs, which Guild factor cries near the mid-span shrine, and why the Choir doubled its order of my anti-static tape in week three. Prices on application.

Rill Davenant owed money in this town too, and paid it the night before she vanished. People who plan to disappear don't settle debts. Whatever she met on the salt, *invite* isn't the word. *Appointment* is.
night: Keel Town at night is all rope-creak and lamp-light, dear. The masts tick. Secrets get heavier after dark — same stock, night surcharge.
I sleep under the shop counter with the drawer open. Nothing's been stolen in eleven years. Word gets around what happens to the adhesively overconfident.
storm: Storm season, dear: everything's discounted except rope. Rope's never discounted.
When the wall comes, I close the drawer first, the shutters second. Priorities are a kind of loyalty.
farewells: Mind your grip, dear. The desert's adhesive is called 'consequence' and I don't sell the solvent.
Come back when you know something. Everyone does, eventually. It's the shop's whole business model.
